name: run_command
description: Look around in your worktree with a shell command: `git branch -r`, `git log --oneline`, `ls`, `cat README.md`, `grep -rn name src`. It runs in the workspace's environment (a run pod of the run's own when the deployment runs them). You get the exit code and the tail of the output. It costs no check cycle and reports no checks, and it is for looking: changes it makes to HEAD, the branch and the working tree are undone and refused (to make a file or change the worktree with a command, use run; to change code, write_file, edit_file or apply_patch). Use it to look; use run_checks only for the project's real checks. Long output is kept: you get its head and tail and an id to read the rest with read_output.

command.description: Shell command, run with `bash -lc` (`sh -lc` without bash) in the worktree, in the workspace's environment

cwd.description: Optional sub-directory of the worktree to run in (relative, inside the worktree)

repo.description: The slot to run in: its name, or the repository's address. Leave out when the workspace has one.

timeout.description: Seconds before the command is killed; at most the deployment's limit, which is also the default. Example: {"command":"npm test","timeout":120}
